taxonomyNote: Species epithet formerly spelled 'platyrhinos'; NatureServe lists it as Eastern Hog-nosed Snake.
fieldMarks: Thick body, wide head and a slightly upturned, pointed snout; adults 45-105 cm.
Juveniles pinkish with alternating dark brown to black blotches.
Adults vary from tan, gray, red, yellowish or greenish to solid dark gray or black; lighter ones show dark blotches.
Belly white to light gray; 23-25 dorsal scale rows and a divided anal plate.
behavior: Diurnal, most active around mid-day; active early April to October/November depending on temperature.
Overwinters in burrows or under talus rocks; lays 4-61 eggs May-August.
habitat: Open wooded hills, forest edges, fields, meadows, prairies, sand plains and river valleys with loose soil and amphibian prey.
range: Southern New England and southern Ontario to Minnesota and South Dakota, south to southern Texas, the Gulf Coast and southern Florida.
